recovered_memory.title: A peer trigger proves coordination, not artifact origin
recovered_memory.summary: An immutable trigger-request record proves that one team requested another team to inspect or continue work at a stated time. It does not assign M-004, M-005, or M-006 to a referent, establish continuity namespace or ownership, prove the semantic role of a missing artifact, or establish temporal origin. Trigger records are therefore coordination evidence and candidate leads only, never origin evidence by themselves.

sources_inspected.observed_state: Five pending requests record cross-team reasons, attempted trigger paths, and execution_claimed=false.

sources_inspected.role: Independent Creative Web continuity trigger-request update

gate_results.reason: The requests coordinate follow-up work but do not assign any unresolved identifier to a referent.
The requests contain team and queue coordination identifiers, not an explicit continuity artifact namespace for M-004, M-005, or M-006.
A requesting or target team is not evidence of the missing artifact's owner.
A trigger request is a coordination record, not a decision log, language lexicon, project artifact, or provenance-bearing artifact assignment.
The inspected requests were recorded after the unresolved artifact reports and contain no immutable back-reference to an originating assignment.
The request ledger updates are retained in immutable repository commits.

candidate_class_adjudication.decision_rule: One passing locator-integrity gate cannot compensate for failed or unevaluated identity gates.

claims.text: The trigger ledger explicitly records request reasons, pending status, direct-trigger outcomes, and execution_claimed=false.
Because the record proves coordination but performs no artifact assignment, it cannot resolve an origin claim under the existing conjunctive adjudication contract.
Future continuity ingestion should classify trigger requests as coordination_evidence by default and require a separate immutable originating object before origin promotion.
A committed trigger request that names a completed slice can serve as provenance for the underlying artifact.
The originating assignment objects for M-004, M-005, and M-006 remain unlocated under exhaustive coverage.

contradiction_resolution.apparent_conflict: A trigger record may contain a precise completed-slice description and an immutable commit while still lacking origin authority.
contradiction_resolution.resolution: Precision and immutability establish what the trigger record says; they do not transform a coordination event into the originating assignment of a different artifact.

next_resolution_step: Exclude trigger-request records from origin promotion, then continue exhaustive branch and pre-boundary commit traversal for explicit assignment objects in eligible source classes.
